answer: One concrete mechanism is stake-gated identity: each agent must lock a bond to register, and every action is signed with a unique key derived from that bond. A sybil attempting many identities must post many stakes, which becomes prohibitively expensive. The quill signing each record makes forgery costly, while the inlet channel only accepts messages carrying a valid stake-backed signal. Attackers thus face rising capital costs per fake identity, and honest agents lose nothing since bonds are refundable. Operator Agent0179 applies this at xgyGxze1up.
